title: Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) for Agents
summary: Quarantine repeatedly failing agent jobs with enough context for diagnosis and controlled replay, keeping poison work from blocking healthy processing.
overview: A dead-letter queue receives work that cannot complete under its configured processing policy. It separates poison messages, persistent validation failures, and exhausted retries from the main queue so healthy work can continue. The DLQ is an operational work queue, not a permanent trash bin or a substitute for error classification.

Retain the original business operation identity, payload reference, attempt history, failure reason, and software versions. Replay must preserve idempotency and revalidate current authorization and schema compatibility. Queue-specific semantics matter: redrive thresholds, retention, ordering, and timestamps are provider-dependent and should be tested for the selected queue type.

production.poc: A prototype can move a deliberately malformed job aside after a bounded number of attempts. Confirm that operators can identify why it failed.
production.production: Production defines retryable versus terminal errors, DLQ ownership, alerts, retention, and safe redrive procedures. Sensitive payloads should remain protected even when copied into diagnostic queues.
production.scale: At scale, group failures by signature and deploy targeted fixes before replaying large batches. Uncontrolled redrive can recreate the original outage or overload a newly recovered dependency.

components.name: Primary work queue
components.role: Delivers accepted agent jobs under documented visibility and redelivery semantics.

components.name: Failure classifier
components.role: Determines whether another attempt is useful or the job should be quarantined.

components.name: Dead-letter store
components.role: Retains failed work with operation identity, evidence references, and diagnostic metadata.

components.name: Triage console
components.role: Supports ownership, grouping, inspection, and disposition of failed jobs.

components.name: Redrive controller
components.role: Revalidates and requeues selected jobs with rate limits and preserved idempotency.

flow.title: Attempt bounded processing
flow.description: Claim a job and apply the workflow's deadline, retry, and idempotency controls.

flow.title: Classify failure
flow.description: Distinguish transient dependency errors from invalid payloads, denied actions, and exhausted attempts.

flow.title: Quarantine durably
flow.description: Preserve the job and failure metadata before removing it from ordinary processing.

flow.title: Notify accountable owner
flow.description: Alert on age, volume, or critical job classes rather than only raw queue size.

flow.title: Repair and validate
flow.description: Correct code, data, or configuration and test representative failed cases.

flow.title: Redrive carefully
flow.description: Replay selected jobs under current policy and rate limits, retaining their business operation identities.

useCase.title: Recovering failed invoice ingestion jobs
useCase.situation: A distributor ingests supplier invoices through an agent that extracts fields and reconciles purchase-order references.
useCase.problem: A supplier changes its document format, causing the same jobs to fail repeatedly and consume the main worker pool.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must isolate affected invoices while continuing to process valid suppliers and preserving recovery evidence.
useCase.architecture: The queue policy sends persistent extraction failures to a protected DLQ with document references, parser versions, and operation keys.
runtime: Operations staff group failures by supplier format and validate a parser correction on representative samples.
The redrive controller requeues the affected invoices gradually using their original operation identities.
useCase.failure: If an invoice already created a payable before a later stage failed, replay reconciles that payable and resumes incomplete work rather than creating another.
useCase.impact: Track oldest failed job, failure signatures, successful redrive, duplicate-effect prevention, and business backlog age.

tradeoffs.benefit: Poison jobs stop consuming ordinary processing capacity.
tradeoffs.cost: Operators need ownership and tooling to resolve the backlog.

tradeoffs.benefit: Root causes can be grouped and reproduced.
tradeoffs.cost: Diagnostic data increases storage and privacy responsibilities.
Excessive replay rate can overload dependencies or repeat systemic failure.

failures.scenario: The DLQ has no owner and jobs expire
failures.detection: Age monitoring shows unresolved work approaching retention limits.
failures.recovery: Assign business ownership and disposition before evidence is lost.

failures.scenario: Redrive repeats an already committed command
failures.detection: Operation ledger shows an existing effect.
failures.recovery: Reuse that result and resume only incomplete stages.

mistakes.mistake: Treating all failures as retryable until exhaustion

mistakes.fix: Preserve business identity across every delivery.

mistakes.mistake: Redriving the entire queue after a deployment
mistakes.fix: Validate representative cases and ramp replay gradually.

whenToUse: Queued jobs can fail persistently or contain poison input.
Healthy work should continue during localized failures.
Failed work has a clear triage and replay owner.
whenNotToUse: The task is synchronous and no durable job exists.
Failures must be returned immediately with no later recovery.
No process exists to inspect or resolve quarantined work.
checklist: Define retryable and terminal failure classes.
Preserve operation identity and diagnostic versions.
Assign DLQ ownership and age alerts.
Set retention beyond expected triage time.
